faq: Why do my ad platform and store show different sales?
Common causes are duplicate firing, missing consent, attribution windows and refunds. We check each cause, fix the ones in our control and explain the rest, so you know what difference is normal.
Which conversions should I track first?
The ones that earn money: purchases, then add to cart or lead forms. We suggest a short list during the first day, based on how your store sells, and avoid cluttering reports with minor clicks.
Can you track sales that happen by phone or in person?
Partly. We can track phone link clicks and form leads on the site. Offline sales need your own data uploaded to the ad platform, which Premium can set up as a simple manual process.
Do I need ad accounts to order this?
No. Basic works with Google Analytics alone. For Standard and Premium we need an ad account you own and add us as a standard user. We never ask for your login password.

desc:
Conversion tracking setup for ecommerce records the actions that matter, such as purchases, sign-ups and quote requests, and sends them to your analytics and ad accounts. Ecom Swift LLC builds and tests each one so your reports match real sales.

## Why does conversion tracking matter for an online store?

Conversion tracking counts the actions that make you money and attaches a value to each. Without it, you see traffic but cannot say which pages, campaigns or products lead to a sale. Ad platforms also run blind, because they optimize toward whatever signal you send them.

When the ad platform says one number and your store says another, every decision becomes an argument. Should you raise the budget, pause the campaign or change the offer? Good tracking replaces that argument with figures you can check against your order list.

## How accurate conversions change your results

Ad systems steer spend toward the people most likely to repeat the action you track. If you track only page views, they find people who browse. If you track purchases with the right value, they find people who buy, and they can favor higher-value orders. The quality of the signal sets the quality of the traffic you buy.

Reporting changes too. With sign-ups, form leads and phone clicks tracked next to purchases, you can see which landing pages and campaigns start the journey and which finish it. Order value and currency show revenue by channel, not just counts. Refund handling keeps the revenue line honest when orders are returned.

Duplicates do the opposite. A purchase counted twice inflates revenue, flatters campaigns and teaches ad platforms the wrong pattern. Catching that early is much of the value.

## What strong conversion tracking includes

- A written list of conversions, each with a name, a trigger and a reason it exists.
- A purchase conversion in Google Analytics with order ID, value and currency.
- Protection against the thank-you page being reloaded and counted again.
- Lead conversions for sign-ups, contact forms, quote requests and booking buttons.
- Click tracking for phone numbers, email links and key buttons.
- Matching conversions in each connected ad platform, using the same rules.
- A server-side purchase signal where the platform supports one.
- Conversion values that reflect real worth, including a plan for refunds.
- A comparison of tracked orders with orders in the store.

## How we set up and test your conversions

We begin with a short conversation about what counts as success for your business. A store may treat the purchase as the main conversion, with newsletter sign-ups as a smaller one. A service business may care most about quote requests and calls.

Then we build each conversion in Google Analytics and mark it as a key event. Where you advertise, we create matching conversions in the ad platform and connect them, so the same action is counted once, with the same value. We use Google Tag Manager or your platform's built-in tools, whichever keeps your site cleaner.

Testing comes next. We place a real order, submit real forms and click real buttons, then check that each action appears once in Analytics, once in the ad platform and once in your store. In the Basic package we focus on the purchase. Standard adds more conversions and one ad platform. Premium covers several platforms, server-side signals, value rules, refund handling, a matching check and a walkthrough call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Track fewer, clearer conversions rather than everything you can.
- Send value and currency with every purchase.
- Use the order ID so repeats can be spotted.
- Compare tracked totals with the store each month.
- Record every change in a short log.

**Avoid:**
- Counting page views of a thank-you page as proof of a sale.
- Marking every click as a conversion.
- Letting two tools report the same purchase to one ad account.
- Ignoring refunds when you judge campaign returns.
- Changing the checkout without retesting the tags.

## Who conversion tracking is for

This service suits store owners whose ad dashboards and sales reports tell different stories. It also fits businesses that generate leads rather than carts, such as local services, course sellers and quote-based shops. Brands about to scale ad spend benefit most, since small tracking faults grow as budgets do.

Some sales happen away from the site, by phone or in person. We can discuss how to bring those into your reports, though such sales need information from you.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you want to track, which ad platforms you use, and what each conversion is worth to you. We need access to your store, your analytics property, your tag manager if you have one, and your ad accounts, given as collaborator, staff, editor or user roles. We do not ask for passwords. A recent order number helps us check that tracked sales match the store.
